title: Spinach, canned, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned spinach cooked with butter or margarine consists of finely chopped spinach leaves that have been heat‑treated and sealed in airtight jars. Butter or margarine is added during cooking, enhancing flavor and increasing the product’s energy content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach is high in iron, and its bioavailability improves when cooked with fats.
Thermal processing preserves most B‑vitamins, while some vitamin C is lost.
In the United States canned spinach is a common ingredient in casseroles, omelets, and soups.
Adding butter or margarine boosts the levels of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K.
Leafy spinach was first cultivated in Persia over 2,000 years ago.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Iron from spinach supports hemoglobin formation and helps maintain energy levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains beta‑carotene (vitamin A)
items.content: Beta‑carotene promotes healthy vision, immune function, and skin.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in spinach aids regular bowel movements.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Spinach contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergy to added fats
items.content: Some individuals may react to the butter or margarine used in preparation.

items.title: Heat‑induced vitamin C loss
items.content: Vitamin C is partially degraded during canning, so the product is not a primary source of this vitamin.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the canned spinach in the microwave or on the stove, then stir into pasta, omelets, casseroles, or soups. It works well as a quick side dish or as a base for vegetable‑rich meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened jar in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer the contents to an airtight container and refrigerate for 3–4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
